plan.contextChunk: This figure shows the agent–environment interaction loop in reinforcement learning, depicted as a closed directed cycle between two rounded rectangular boxes filled with light teal. The upper box is labeled “Agent” with the policy π[a_t | s_t] inscribed inside, and the lower, larger box is labeled “Environment” with the state transition probability Pr(s_{t+1} | s_t, a_t) inscribed inside. Orange arrows with arrowheads form the loop: one arrow routes from the Agent box rightward and downward into the Environment box, carrying the action a_t; a second arrow returns from the Environment to the Agent carrying the current state s_t, while a third routes the next state s_{t+1} back around; additional arrow paths carry rewards r_t and r_{t+1}, and a label identifies the reward function Pr(r_{t+1} | s_t, a_t). Small white-background rectangles along the arrow paths isolate variable labels — State, Action, and Reward — for readability. This figure introduces the Markov Decision Process (MDP) framework at the core of reinforcement learning, showing how the agent observes a state, selects an action according to its policy, and receives a reward and next state from the environment in a repeating closed loop.

interactionPlan.concept: Reinforcement learning is a closed loop: the agent observes state s_t, picks an action a_t via its policy π[a_t|s_t], and the environment responds with a reward r_{t+1} and next state s_{t+1} according to its transition and reward distributions.

Environment box: larger rounded rectangle, light teal fill, lower area, labeled 'Environment' with 'State transition Pr(s_{t+1}|s_t, a_t)' and 'Reward function Pr(r_{t+1}|s_t, a_t)' inside

orange arrow from Environment routing right/up back to Agent, labeled 'State s_t'

dashed vertical line on the left separating time t from t+1
small white-background label rectangles isolating 'State', 'Action', 'Reward' text along the arrow paths

interactions.label: Play one MDP time step
interactions.teaches: The causal order of one time step: s_t leaves the environment, enters the agent, the policy emits a_t, and the environment returns r_{t+1} and s_{t+1} — the loop is a repeating cycle, not a one-way pipeline
The agent's only job is the policy π[a_t|s_t]: it maps the observed state to the action arrow a_t — highlighting both together shows the policy is what connects state in to action out

The environment owns two distributions — the state transition Pr(s_{t+1}|s_t,a_t) and the reward function Pr(r_{t+1}|s_t,a_t) — both conditioned on the same (s_t, a_t) pair, which is the Markov property

demo_steps.title: The closed loop
demo_steps.narration: Two boxes, one cycle: the agent and environment exchange states, actions, and rewards forever. Play the animation to watch one full time step traverse the loop in order.

demo_steps.title: What the agent does
demo_steps.narration: Click the Agent box: the policy π[a_t|s_t] and the outgoing action arrow light up together — the agent is nothing more than a state-to-action mapping.

demo_steps.title: What the environment does
demo_steps.narration: Click the Environment box: both the transition and reward distributions highlight — both depend only on the current (s_t, a_t), which is exactly the Markov property that makes this an MDP.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: Everything in an MDP is conditioned only on the current state and action: the agent's policy turns s_t into a_t, and the environment turns (s_t, a_t) into r_{t+1} and s_{t+1} — history never matters, and the loop repeats.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Two rounded rectangles with light teal fill and dark outlines: smaller 'Agent' box top-center containing 'Policy π[a_t|s_t]'; larger 'Environment' box bottom-center containing 'State transition Pr(s_{t+1}|s_t, a_t)' and 'Reward function Pr(r_{t+1}|s_t, a_t)'. Orange arrows with filled arrowheads route around the boxes in rectangular elbows: action a_t exits the agent's right side and enters the environment's right side; state s_t returns on the right; on the left, reward r_t and state s_t flow up into the agent, while s_{t+1} and r_{t+1} labels sit just right of a vertical dashed line marking the t → t+1 boundary. Labels 'State s_t', 'Action a_t', 'Reward r_t' sit on small white rectangles that knock out the arrow lines beneath them. Math labels in italic serif. Animation should pulse a highlight along each arrow segment in sequence (s_t → agent → a_t → environment → r_{t+1}, s_{t+1}); clicks highlight the box interior text plus its associated arrows in a warm accent color.

discrepancies: The s_{t+1} label beside the dashed separator is drawn overlapping/through the dashed line, whereas in the source it sits cleanly to the left of the line above r_{t+1}

In the source the two arrows into the Agent (reward r_t and state s_t) enter the left side at two distinct heights with visible arrowheads; the generated reward arrow enters at the box's top-left corner and the state arrow at mid-left, slightly compressing the visual separation of the two inputs
The right-side 'State s_t' return line in the generated figure merges into the left riser without an arrowhead, while the source shows the state line as a continuous path back toward the agent

The action arrow on the right side is thinner and the far-right vertical run sits further left than the source's wide 'Action a_t' drop, making the right column labels ('State s_t' / 'Action a_t') crowd the wires
evaluation.notes: The generated figure reproduces the classic MDP agent–environment loop with correct boxes, equations, elbow arrows, labels, and colors, and adds a genuinely useful time-step animation, highlightable boxes with informative popups, and a 3-step narration player; only minor routing and one label-overlap issue distinguish it from the source.
action_items: Move the s_{t+1} label left a few pixels (or extend its white knockout) so it does not sit on top of the dashed time separator.

Route the reward arrow into the top-left edge of the Agent box at a clearly distinct height from the state arrow, and give both right-side and left-side return paths consistent arrowhead treatment matching the source.
Spread the right-side 'State s_t' and 'Action a_t' labels further apart horizontally to match the source's wider right column.

feedback.rationale: Scores are high (average 4.4, concept and interactivity at 5), failure modes are empty, and the remaining discrepancies are trivial polish issues like a label overlap and arrow routing that do not impair understanding — iteration cost outweighs marginal gain.
